title: The grader with codes, the first variant family and the baseline (harness learning, H0)
request: The owner asked to start building H0 of the harness-learning plan: the challenge pack contract, the grader with codes, the first variant family and the scoreboard baseline, then stop.
spec: Plan 'improve the harness so it learns', package H0 (Phase 9's 31.1 to 31.4, revised by the two harness reports): a pack's public part and its key apart; a deterministic grader whose codes never name a column (the lesson leak the reports found in Phase 9's example); the duplicate and group leakage family in learning, check and sealed partitions; today's DCLab as the zero of every learning curve.
plan: read the kinds' cases and acceptance runs, the replicas, the engine's records, the campaigns' layout and the contract registry
the contracts in dclab_core (challenge_pack: pack, key, observed, grade) with the code vocabulary and the partition rule
the groups family generator with its knobs and the reference statements
the studio side: packs written apart from their keys, a solve from the public folder, observe a run
the scoreboard: two arms per variant as a run of the learning agent, the summary, the sealed rule, the campaign and the make target
tests, the baselines on check and learning, the adversarial review

decisions.decision: The new contract is challenge_pack, not challenge
decisions.why: dclab_core.challenge and dclab_rnd.challenge already name 16.13's challenge mode (briefs)

decisions.decision: Codes name a kind of mistake and its trap (SPLIT_WRONG:repeated_entity), never a column or a value
decisions.why: a lesson written from a code cannot carry one variant's answer to the next; the reports found that leak in Phase 9's own lesson example

decisions.decision: Duplicates are a knob, not a graded trap
decisions.why: the engine reports duplicates only in a note no statement can change, so even the right answer would fail a duplicate check; copies are an entity's rows, which the group split holds

decisions.decision: The honest-estimate guard uses the holdout's own bootstrap interval, a fixed share only as a fallback
decisions.why: with about 40 groups in the holdout an honest estimate missed a fixed 5% limit by chance: the reference failed 2 of 12 variants

decisions.decision: Every variant must pass with its key's statements, or it is dropped and listed
decisions.why: a variant the right answer cannot pass measures the generator, not the solver

decisions.decision: The baselines run on check and learning; the sealed partition stays unread
decisions.why: a sealed set is read once per promotion, where both arms run paired on it; a baseline read now would spend it for nothing

decisions.decision: Each attempt is a run of a new harness agent, learning, each arm a step with its whole grade
decisions.why: the owner's rule: every process records itself; the harness test requires every agent registered with a probe

change: dclab_core/challenge_pack.py (new), dclab_core/variants.py (new), dclab_core/contracts.py (registered), dclab_core 0.102.0 + CHANGELOG + schemas and baselines; dclab_rnd/learning/ (new: packs, grading, scoreboard, __main__); dclab_rnd/agents/harness.py (the learning agent); Makefile (learning-baseline); evidence/campaigns/learning_v1/manifest.json; docs/DATA_CATALOG.md and data_catalog.json regenerated; tests/test_learning_h0.py (new), tests/test_agent_harness.py (its probe).

findings.defect: the first variants were unsolvable: most of the signal sat in the entity's hidden risk, so even the reference answer barely beat the baseline (AUC 0.59; for regression worse than the median)
findings.cause: a generator that put the trap's signal where no honest model can reach it
findings.fix: row-level features carry their own signal (amount, item count, tier, channel) beside the entity's risk
findings.impact: every variant would have been dropped as unsolvable

findings.defect: a timed variant broke the engine: every entity recurred across the year, so a split both forward in time and by entity left 2 rows to test on
findings.cause: entities active all year, unlike real customers and patients
findings.fix: each entity is active in a window of weeks; a time-and-group split then holds out entities it never saw
alternatives: grade timed variants on the time split alone (drops the family's trap)

findings.defect: a fixed 5% gap limit failed honest solves
findings.scenario: 2 of 12 reference solves failed GAP_OPTIMISTIC on holdouts of about 40 groups
findings.cause: sampling noise of a small grouped holdout is larger than a fixed share
findings.fix: the guard reads the holdout's bootstrap interval; 0 of 30 reference failures after
findings.impact: a grader that fails right answers

findings.defect: the public pack carried its seed (its id, a field, the row keys' values), so whoever could run the generator could rebuild the key without opening it
findings.cause: a deterministic id from the seed
findings.fix: an opaque token as the id; seed and partition moved into the key; row keys drawn at random from the seed's generator, never its digits
findings.impact: the key readable by a solver that runs code
findings.open: a solver that runs the generator could still match a table by brute force over seeds: H1's sandbox is where that closes

findings.defect: a solve that never fitted a model passed: the guards were skipped when a score was missing
findings.scenario: Observed with the right columns kept out and no scores
findings.cause: a guard ran only when its numbers existed
findings.fix: a missing validation, holdout or baseline fails its guard
findings.impact: a free pass for doing nothing

findings.defect: keeping every honest column out went unpunished when a variant had no decoy (four in ten)
findings.scenario: all honest columns but one blocked: holdout 0.55 against 0.5 passed
findings.cause: only decoys were checked for false alarms
findings.fix: the key lists the honest columns known before the moment; keeping any out is a false alarm

findings.defect: the sealed rule could be bypassed: a run without --write, or one that crashed, left no file and the next read was allowed
findings.scenario: baseline --split sealed without --write, again and again
findings.cause: the check looked for a stored result only
findings.fix: a sealed read must be stored, and its marker is written before the first solve; a broken attempt is a row with its reason

findings.defect: the run record was cut before the codes and held column names; the command installed no record at all
findings.scenario: a learning session's tool result cut at 360 characters inside its checks
findings.cause: the whole grade and observed were the step's result; no log was installed by the CLI
findings.fix: a step keeps the verdict and the codes only; the command installs the workspace's record; the session's params name the pack and partition
findings.impact: an attempt not captured whole; names a learner would read

findings.defect: the reference arm, which states the key's answers, could write them to a ledger as a person's decisions
findings.scenario: a server or self-play ledger installed during a baseline
findings.cause: acceptance's adopt records the solution as a person's
findings.fix: the reference arm runs with no ledger and records no events

findings.defect: the table's SHA-256 was of the frame in memory, not of the file a solver reads
findings.scenario: nobody could check table.csv against the pack
findings.fix: the SHA-256 of the CSV's exact bytes, and exactly those bytes written
findings.impact: a fingerprint no one could verify

findings.defect: names_in matched substrings and missed names written with spaces
findings.fix: whole words, with underscores or spaces
findings.impact: H2's name filter would have been wrong

findings.defect: a result file of another family ending in the same name refused a sealed run, and two runs could take one id; the decoy ignored time order
findings.scenario: glob LRN-*_groups_sealed; a decoy counted before the sort by time
findings.cause: a loose pattern, a read-then-write id, a count before the sort
findings.fix: an exact pattern, open(..., 'x') with a retry, the count after the sort
findings.impact: rare collisions and a decoy out of order

findings.defect: the honesty guard still failed an honest solve after the two-noise fix
findings.scenario: a regression variant on 57 groups: validation beat the holdout by 2.7 noise units with the reference answer
findings.cause: the engine's holdout intervals run narrow on small grouped holdouts (40 draws)
findings.fix: the threshold measured, not guessed: 60 honest reference solves on learning and check variants reached 2.71 at most; the guard fails past 3.5, the gaming traces sit at 5 to 8
findings.impact: a grader that fails right answers

measurements.name: the reference arm on 60 variants (30 learning, 30 check)
measurements.gate: every variant solvable by its key's statements; the honesty guard's threshold set above every honest solve
measurements.result: 60 of 60 solvable; the largest honest gap 2.71 noise units, 2 of 60 past 1.96; the threshold set at 3.5 before the baselines

measurements.name: the baselines (LRN-001 check, LRN-002 learning; 20 variants each)
measurements.result: check: today's DCLab passes 7 of 20 (Wilson 0.18 to 0.57), decision score 0.86; learning: 3 of 20 (0.05 to 0.36), 0.83; all 40 solvable; it fails a plain-named group key in 0 of 19 and a decoy in 0 of 24; it catches the leak in all 40
measurements.next: H1, the read-only layer; the sealed partition stays unread until the first promotion
limits: the leak is nearly perfect, so a one-column screen finds it whatever its name: the leak_name knob does not make it harder
the sealed variants come from the same generator; an independent author is the owner's decision
no converter from today's replicas yet: the plan's H0 named it; it follows

outcome: A challenge pack lives apart from its key, a solve reads only the public part, a deterministic grader returns codes that never name a column, the groups family draws distinct and solvable variants in three partitions, and today's DCLab is measured on them as the zero of every learning curve.
lessons: Prove a generated challenge solvable by its own key before counting it: a variant the right answer fails measures the generator.
Judge an estimate against its own sampling interval, not a fixed share.
risks: the sealed variants are drawn by the same generator as the learning ones: a learner that fits the generator's habits could pass them; an independent author is the plan's open decision
the grader judges decisions, not a fresh holdout of unseen entities: a solve that splits right but models badly passes when it beats the baseline
a solver that can run the generator could match a table to its seed by brute force: closed only by H1's sandbox
the replica converter and the 'every replica grades as today' test are not built (named in the plan's H0)
